preserve: An addressed resource call reaches its independently authenticated owner with its original operation, input and request key; protocol framing does not supply account authority.
Successful tool results and owner refusals remain structured MCP results. A refusal retains its owner-supplied code and effect state while protected declarations and withheld answers stay private.
Effect observations belong to the current server request, never arbitrary client metadata. A failure after dispatch cannot imply that the effect did not start or authorize a duplicate effect.
allowed_deltas: The Rust rmcp SDK owns JSON-RPC negotiation and Streamable HTTP framing. This is an explicit adaptation from the retired JavaScript handler, not a claim of literal source copying, MCP batch parity or complete protocol parity.

The existing Rust OperationFailure classifier supplies one effect-state interpretation to shared refusal encoding and SDK overflow classification. Its private committed declaration and uncertainty-dominates rules are explicit adaptations, not fields claimed to exist in the old JavaScript result.

An existing admitted HTTP request supplies VerifiedRequest through request extensions. SDK initialization discloses only that verified account and resource work refuses without that request witness; the SDK service factory adds no authentication or session owner.

A bounded reply that overflows after a resource may have acted remains outcome unknown. The SDK adaptation reuses the existing bounded encoders and shared effect classifier rather than reporting not_started because protocol framing failed.
banned_substitutions: A caller field, nested detail value or failure code name used to declare a committed effect.
A post-effect overflow encoded as a known not-started refusal, a duplicate dispatch, or disclosure of the private effect declaration/withheld answer.
A claim that these seven source tests prove installed behavior, the native mcp_local consumer mapping, batch parity or complete MCP protocol parity.
An invented retirement, SOURCE_FIRST_PORT/byte-copy ancestry, or NO_PRIOR_OWNER claim.
